explication: AndroidMic turns an Android phone into a PC microphone. The user configures both apps, grants recording access, and starts a connection; Android captures microphone samples, selects WiFi or USB transport, and sends packets to the desktop. The desktop receives them, converts and processes audio, then plays it through a selected virtual audio cable for other applications. The tree and excerpts clearly support the service, transport choices, desktop UI, configuration, and audio-processing layers; some lower-level runner wiring is represented conservatively.
